newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB outlines US$750 mln debt issue.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB outlines US$750 mln debt issue.

text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd said on Thursday the previously announced capital raising of up to US$750 million would be issued in the form of a debt security, exchangable for equity or cash.

"As part of our active capital management programme, we announced last November our intention to issue new capital instrument to raise up US$750 million," chairman William Irvine told the bank's annual meeting.

"The instrument would be issued in the form of debt security qualifying as tier two capital and will be exchangable at the option of the bank for perpetual convertible preference shares of the bank qualifying as tier one capital," Irvine said.
"The instrument would also be exchangable, at the option of the investor, for ordinary shares in the bank, or at the bank's election, for cash," Irvine said.

Irvine said new securities would be redeemable after 10 years, subject to central bank approval. The preference shares would not be redeemable but could be bought back after 10 years or converted to ordinary shares at a premium, he said.
The capital raising was announced in conjunction with a A$1.1 billion share buy-back. Both initiatives were aimed at benefitting Australian-based shareholders, the bank said.

"This new cost effective capital raising will provide the group with greater flexibility to manage its capital improve access to the international capital markets, and would broaden the investor base consistent with the group's international expansion," Irvine said.
